statutes.act: Read With Section 148 Ipc And Under Section 27 Of The Arms Act

facts: On a report made by Jugeshwar Singh [PW-7] alleging that the appellants herein along with several other persons numbering about 20 came to 'Khalihan' [threshing floor] of Bhola Singh where he and other members of his family were threshing paddy.
They tried to take away the paddy. Upendra Singh threatened that any resistance would be met with such action which might even result in death.
Thereafter Rajendra Singh hit Bhola Singh with a lathi and Upendra Singh moved backward and fired at Bhola Singh with gun as a result of which Bhola Singh was hit and fell down writhing in pain.

Saryu Singh was shot at by Rajendra Singh and Bhagwat Dayal Singh, who was also inflicted a bhala blow by Arvind Singh, appellant in the connected matter, Umed Singh and Sheonandan Singh fired at Rajdeo Singh as a result of which he fell down.

When Dharmshila, wife of Bhola Singh reached the threshing floor with her child aged about one and half years old in her arm named Rinku, Sheonandan Singh snatched the child and threw the child on the ground as a result of which the child died.
issues: Intent to cause death or grievous hurt
petitioner_arguments: The appellants did not intend to cause death or grievous hurt.
The common objective was only to take away paddy from the threshing floor and it was not that it should be one to cause injuries much less than death to anyone.
Rajendra Singh gave a blow with lathi to Bhola Singh, he could not have intended his death.
respondent_arguments: The appellants were members of an unlawful assembly which was armed with lathis and guns and a declaration had been made that in the event there is any resistance to take away the paddy, they were willing to take life out of the deceased and take away the paddy.
court_reasoning: The prosecution has established that the appellants were members of an unlawful assembly which was armed with lathis and guns and a declaration had been made that in the event there is any resistance to take away the paddy, they were willing to take life out of the deceased and take away the paddy.
Everyone must be taken to have intended the probable and natural results of the combination of the acts in which he had joined.
holding: The appeals filed by Umesh Singh and Rajendra Singh are dismissed.
Arvind Singh's appeal is allowed in part. His conviction is confirmed but the sentence imposed upon him stands set aside. He is, therefore, set at liberty, if not required in any other case.
